title: Arsenal turn down Al-Ittihad approach for Belgium forward Leandro Trossard
trail: The Saudi Arabian club offered £4m to loan the 29-year-old before the Pro League transfer window closes on Monday night
body: Arsenal have rejected a late attempt from Al-Ittihad to sign Leandro Trossard on an initial season’s loan and insisted they have no intention of allowing the Belgium forward to leave. The Saudi Arabian club are understood to have proposed to pay £4m to take Trossard on loan with an obligation to make the deal permanent for about £25m. But that was quickly dismissed by Arsenal, who view the 29-year-old as a vital member of their squad despite signing Raheem Sterling on loan from Chelsea on the final day of the Premier League’s transfer window on Friday. The window in Saudi Arabia’s Pro League and several leagues in Europe closes on Monday, and Al-Ittihad hoped Trossard would join Moussa Diaby – who signed from Aston Villa for €60m – in their squad. Trossard started against his former club Brighton on Saturday, having scored the opening goal in Arsenal’s win over Villa as a substitute the previous week. His muted celebration hinted he was not happy at being on the bench, and Mikel Arteta, the Arsenal manager, praised Trossard’s response. Meanwhile, the Napoli striker Victor Osimhen - who was linked with a big-money transfer to England and Saudi Arabia this summer - has agreed a surprise season-long loan move to Galatasaray. The deal, which will see the Turkish champions cover Osimhen’s salary, includes a break clause in January. The former Manchester United defender Chris Smalling also completed a move from Roma to the Saudi Pro League club Al-Fayha on Monday. The window also remains open in the Netherlands and Portugal until Monday night. Manchester City’s Issa Kaboré has joined Benfica on a season’s loan and PSV look set to sign Joel Ndala from City’s academy on loan with an obligation to buy for up to £8.4m, with a buyback clause for the England Under-17 forward understood to have been included in the deal.
